title: Treasury and Liquidity
answer: Cash forecasting, currency hedging, idle cash, bank reconciliation and stress testing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Cash Flow Forecasting
children.blurb: Cash flow forecasting covers the projection of cash receipts and payments across defined time horizons, from intraday balances to weekly, monthly, and quarterly views.

children.name: Currency Hedging
children.blurb: Currency hedging is the practice of managing the impact of exchange rate movements on a company's cash flows, earnings, and balance sheet.

children.name: Idle Cash and Short-Term Yield
children.blurb: Idle cash and short-term yield covers the cash a company holds beyond its immediate operating needs, and the instruments and accounts used to put that cash to work for days, weeks or months.

children.name: Bank Reconciliation
children.blurb: Bank reconciliation is the process of comparing a company's internal cash records with bank statements to confirm that payments, receipts, fees, and interest are recorded correctly and that the ending balances agree.

children.name: Liquidity Stress Testing
children.blurb: Liquidity stress testing is the practice of projecting a firm's cash inflows and outflows under adverse scenarios to see whether it can meet obligations as they fall due.

sections.body: Treasury and liquidity is the part of finance that keeps cash moving, matches incoming and outgoing payments, and makes sure a company can meet obligations as they fall due. AI is now used in cash flow forecasting to read bank feeds, invoices, payroll schedules and sales pipelines, then produce rolling forecasts that update more often than a monthly spreadsheet. In currency hedging, models help estimate exposure from receivables, payables and intercompany flows, and they can suggest hedge ratios or timing, though a human still approves trades. For idle cash and short term yield, systems scan balances across accounts and compare short term instruments, but they do not remove the need to check credit quality and liquidity terms. Bank reconciliation uses matching algorithms to pair ledger entries with bank statements, flag breaks and learn from prior corrections. Liquidity stress testing uses scenario engines to shock cash inflows and outflows, then report where buffers might fail under assumed conditions.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Much of the daily work is solved at the level of data capture and matching, because bank feeds, APIs and reconciliation engines can handle high volumes with fewer manual touches. Forecasting remains partly unsolved, especially for irregular receipts, seasonality, multi currency flows and sudden changes in customer behavior, where models can be confident and wrong. Hedging is not a prediction problem alone, because accounting rules, hedge documentation and risk mandates constrain what any model may recommend. Idle cash optimization is limited by counterparty limits, settlement timing and the simple fact that yield and safety trade off against each other. Stress testing is only as good as the scenarios and the data lineage behind them, and many firms still run a small number of historical or hypothetical shocks rather than a full live simulation. The honest limit is that AI can improve speed, coverage and consistency, but it does not make cash certain, and it does not take responsibility for treasury decisions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Cash Flow Forecasting is the natural starting point, because it sets the expected cash position that the other pages depend on. Currency Hedging follows for readers who need to understand how forecast exposures are translated into hedge decisions and how AI supports exposure netting and trade timing. Idle Cash and Short-Term Yield looks at the asset side, where surplus balances are pooled, compared and monitored against policy limits. Bank Reconciliation is the operational foundation, since clean matching between bank and ledger data is what makes forecasts and liquidity views trustworthy. Liquidity Stress Testing is the page for downside work, where scenarios are applied to the forecast and the balance sheet to see where shortfalls could appear. For definitions of the terms used across these pages, the site's 686 glossary terms are the place to start.
